newsitem.title: LEBANON: Net profits of Beirut Transorient bank up in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Net profits of Beirut Transorient bank up in 1996.

text.p: Lebanon's Transorient bank reported on Tuesday rises in net profits, assets and customer deposits in its audited 1996 financial results.
The results issued in Beirut newspapers said net profits rose 4.9 percent to 7.128 billion Lebanese pounds from 6.795 billion pounds at the end of 1995.
"The 1996 results were very satisfactory as actual return on asset was 2.2 percent and return on equity was around 28 percent," Assistant General Manager Charbel Moubarak told Reuters.
The bank twice increased its capital bringing it to 17.280 billion pounds in 1996 from 2.160 billion a year earlier.
"We have twice increased our capital. Half the increase was realised through cash contribution while the other half was taken out of profit and provisions," Moubarak said.
"We will be continuously increasing our capital. If you don't expand your capital base, you will not be able to survive in this competitive market," he added.
Transorient assets rose 52 percent to 466.936 billion pounds and customer deposits rose by 49 percent to 373.393 billion pounds.

The increases brought the bank's 1996 ranking among Lebanon's 82 commercial banks to 20, 21, and 17 respectively in terms of assets, deposits and net profits. This compared to rankings of 22, 22 and 17 a year earlier.
Moubarak said the bank launched an administrative and operational re-engineering scheme in mid-1995.
"Our strategy focuses on meeting customer needs, balancing risks and return and enhancing systems to ensure continuous innovation," he said.
